decisions.reason: The breakpoint prevents responsive overlap but does not change the candidate's requirement that the first hero sentence receive emphasis rather than the tagline.
The source adds a landing-page-specific breakpoint to solve hero overlap; it does not revise the reusable general breakpoint guidance.
The responsive breakpoint does not change the selected visual concepts, theme, colors, or typography.
The source changes responsive layout behavior, not the shared dark-theme decision for website pages.
Preventing hero text and image overlap does not alter the landing-page sections, their order, or their content.
The breakpoint decision does not change whether the landing page requires a sign-up button.
Adding a breakpoint in styles.css is compatible with the existing plain HTML and Tailwind build decision and does not replace or revise that stack.
The landing-page hero breakpoint does not necessarily affect the Cognito sign-in page's branding, required elements, or background treatment.
The responsive hero-layout change does not alter the decision to omit navigation from the landing-page header.
The breakpoint applies to the landing-page hero and does not change the separate admin-workspace shell styling requirement.
The landing-page breakpoint does not revise the provisioning wizard's layout variables, responsive gaps, or other styling values.
The breakpoint addresses overlap in the hero section and does not change the shared footer's content, navigation, or layout requirements.
